Chapter 14: Rethinking Prosperity—Beyond GDP and the Numbers Game
For as long as most of us can remember, Gross Domestic Product—GDP—has been the go-to way to measure progress. The bigger the number, the better off we’re supposed to be, right? But here’s the thing: those numbers don’t always capture what really matters in life.
Imagine a family whose income goes up, but at the same time, their neighborhood just doesn’t feel as safe anymore. Maybe the air’s getting harder to breathe, and the close-knit community they once had is starting to fade away. On paper, the statistics say this family is better off. But if you ask them, their own experience tells a very different story.
Most folks never really question the limits of economic numbers. Did you know GDP counts all kinds of spending as good—whether it’s putting money into schools or paying to clean up pollution? It completely ignores things like caring for kids or looking after aging parents, even though those are some of the most important jobs out there. And let’s not forget—GDP doesn’t measure happiness, health, or that feeling of hope for the future.
The good news? Some countries are starting to think differently. They’re looking beyond GDP, trying to measure things like well-being, sustainability, and how connected their communities feel. And the results? They might surprise you. Sometimes, more isn’t always better. Real prosperity goes way beyond what’s in your bank account.
So, here’s the key takeaway: what we choose to measure shapes what we end up valuing. If we want to build a better society, it’s time to look past the numbers—and start asking ourselves what truly matters.
